caption: Three kids and R7 200 on groceries. What does your food bill look like with teenagers in the house?

slides.title:
How we spend our
R31 200 household
income
South Africa
Living in Secunda
slides.body:
Him 42, her 39
Married, three kids (15, 13 and 10)
Jobs: Fitter at a plant contractor & school admin clerk
Household net income: R31 200 p/m

slides.title: Bond repayment
slides.includes: 3 bed in Embalenhle, rates and water included
slides.body: We bought when the kids were small. It felt huge then. Now it's three kids and one bathroom.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Five people, packed lunches, a 15 year old who eats twice
slides.body: I used to budget R5 000. Then he turned 15.

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.body: Bought for the school run. We now do the school run in a different car because of the fuel.

slides.title: School fees & uniforms
slides.includes: Two government schools with fees, stationery, sports kit
slides.body: Every term there's a new levy nobody mentioned in January.

slides.title: Friday takeaways
slides.includes: Pizza night and the occasional Nando's
slides.body: We say it's for the kids. It's for us, honestly.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Petrol, hospital plan, electricity, phones, funeral policies, stokvel
slides.body: Five funeral policies adds up quicker than you'd think. It's still the one bill I'd never cut.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R31 200. About R63 a day for a family of five, and one school trip lands on the 15th.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I uploaded two months of statements to Beyond Horizon and it grouped the school costs I'd been scattering across three categories.

Friday takeaways were R400 higher than we thought.

No bank login needed.
